title: Capstone Expo
outcome: By the end, I can defend a complete recommendation with validation, eligibility and reproducible ranking.
scenario: A fictional team presents its transparent book recommender on a reserved catalogue.
given: Request maximum 120 pages; score=2×interest+illustrated, where illustrated is 1 for True and 0 for False; tie by ID.
A pages120 interest3 True; B pages100 interest4 False; C pages121 interest5 True; D pages90 interest"4" True. Numeric fields require exact integers.

steps.label: Validate
steps.detail: D has text interest and is rejected; A,B,C have valid fields.

steps.label: Filter
steps.detail: A and B meet the page limit; C exceeds it.

steps.label: Rank
steps.detail: A scores 7; B scores 8, so B wins.

steps.label: Defend evidence
steps.detail: Explain two eligible items, one page-limit exclusion and one type rejection.

explanation: A presentation should let someone rebuild the result from the stated contract. A’s equality is accepted; D is not silently converted; C’s high preference score cannot override the page requirement. Reversing rows must preserve B because it has the unique highest eligible score. Keep the reserved case distinct from practice demonstrations.

counterfactual.change: An authorised repair converts D’s interest to integer 4.
counterfactual.prediction: D becomes eligible and scores 9, so it wins.
counterfactual.reason: The evidence-backed input repair changes validation and then ranking; record this as a new case/version.

student_task: Give the original winning ID, its score, and counts of eligible, excluded and invalid rows.
teacher_answer: B wins with 8. Two rows eligible, one valid-but-too-long row excluded, one type-invalid row rejected.
project_evidence: Present the Transparent Book Recommender’s code, baseline, full-case traces, reserved results and limitations, without claiming fictional results as pupil work.
limits: A defensible algorithmic trace does not prove B will be liked or that classroom learning improved.
review_note: New fictional case individually matched to this topic, with computations and policy traces checked. Use for supported practice; preserve the independent assessment.
